text: What is a web server? Give one example of web server software.
modelAnswer: A web server is a computer (along with its software) that stores web pages and responds to requests from web browsers by sending the requested pages over the Internet, usually using HTTP/HTTPS. Example: Apache HTTP Server.
keyPoints: A web server is a computer (along with its software) that stores web pages and responds to requests from web browsers by sending the requested pages over the Internet, usually using HTTP/HTTPS.
Example: Apache HTTP Server.

text: Differentiate between downloading and uploading.
modelAnswer: Downloading is the process of copying a file or data from a remote server/computer to one's own local computer. Uploading is the process of sending a file or data from one's own local computer to a remote server/computer. For example, saving a photo from a website is downloading, while posting a photo to a website is uploading.
keyPoints: Downloading is the process of copying a file or data from a remote server/computer to one's own local computer.
Uploading is the process of sending a file or data from one's own local computer to a remote server/computer.
For example, saving a photo from a website is downloading, while posting a photo to a website is uploading.

text: Expand and explain the purpose of SMTP and POP3.
modelAnswer: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used to send outgoing e-mail from a client to a mail server and to relay mail between mail servers. POP3 (Post Office Protocol version 3) is used by an e-mail client to retrieve and download incoming messages from the mail server to the user's device.
keyPoints: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used to send outgoing e-mail from a client to a mail server and to relay mail between mail servers.
POP3 (Post Office Protocol version 3) is used by an e-mail client to retrieve and download incoming messages from the mail server to the user's device.

text: What is the difference between HTTP and HTTPS?
modelAnswer: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) transfers web page data between a browser and a server in plain, unencrypted form. HTTPS (HTTP Secure) is the same protocol enhanced with SSL/TLS encryption, so that data such as passwords or payment details is encrypted during transmission, making it safe from interception.
keyPoints: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) transfers web page data between a browser and a server in plain, unencrypted form.
HTTPS (HTTP Secure) is the same protocol enhanced with SSL/TLS encryption, so that data such as passwords or payment details is encrypted during transmission, making it safe from interception.

text: Name any three remote login/file transfer protocols mentioned in your syllabus and state one use of each.
modelAnswer:
1. SSH (Secure Shell): used for secure, encrypted remote login to another computer.
2. FTP (File Transfer Protocol): used to transfer files between computers over a network, though without encryption.
3. TELNET: used for remote login to another computer over a network, but data is sent unencrypted, making it insecure compared to SSH.
keyPoints: SSH (Secure Shell): used for secure, encrypted remote login to another computer.
FTP (File Transfer Protocol): used to transfer files between computers over a network, though without encryption.
TELNET: used for remote login to another computer over a network, but data is sent unencrypted, making it insecure compared to SSH.

text: Differentiate between SMS and MMS.
modelAnswer: SMS (Short Message Service) allows users to send and receive short text-only messages between mobile phones, traditionally limited to around 160 characters. MMS (Multimedia Messaging Service) extends this by allowing multimedia content such as images, audio clips and video, in addition to text, to be sent between mobile phones.
keyPoints: SMS (Short Message Service) allows users to send and receive short text-only messages between mobile phones, traditionally limited to around 160 characters.

text: Briefly explain the evolution from 3G to 5G mobile technology in terms of capability.
modelAnswer: 3G introduced mobile internet access with moderate speeds sufficient for browsing and video calling. 4G significantly increased data speeds, enabling smooth HD video streaming and heavier mobile applications. 5G further increases speed drastically, reduces latency to near real-time, and supports connecting a very large number of devices simultaneously, enabling applications like IoT and smart cities.
keyPoints: 3G introduced mobile internet access with moderate speeds sufficient for browsing and video calling.
4G significantly increased data speeds, enabling smooth HD video streaming and heavier mobile applications.
5G further increases speed drastically, reduces latency to near real-time, and supports connecting a very large number of devices simultaneously, enabling applications like IoT and smart cities.

text: Differentiate between open source software and proprietary software.
modelAnswer: Open source software makes its source code freely available, allowing users to view, modify and redistribute it, often at no cost (e.g., Linux). Proprietary software is owned by a company, its source code is kept private, and its use is restricted by a paid license that does not allow modification or free redistribution (e.g., licensed versions of MS Office).
keyPoints: Open source software makes its source code freely available, allowing users to view, modify and redistribute it, often at no cost (e.g., Linux).

Proprietary software is owned by a company, its source code is kept private, and its use is restricted by a paid license that does not allow modification or free redistribution (e.g., licensed versions of MS Office).

text: What is plagiarism? Why is it considered unethical?
modelAnswer: Plagiarism is the act of copying or using someone else's work, ideas or words and presenting them as one's own original work without giving proper credit to the original creator. It is unethical because it violates the intellectual property rights of the original author, is a form of academic and professional dishonesty, and can result in loss of trust, penalties, or legal action.
keyPoints: Plagiarism is the act of copying or using someone else's work, ideas or words and presenting them as one's own original work without giving proper credit to the original creator.

It is unethical because it violates the intellectual property rights of the original author, is a form of academic and professional dishonesty, and can result in loss of trust, penalties, or legal action.

text: Differentiate between copyright, trademark and patent.
modelAnswer: Copyright protects original literary, artistic, musical or software works, giving the creator exclusive rights over reproduction and distribution. A trademark protects distinctive brand names, logos or symbols that identify a company's goods or services. A patent protects new inventions, giving the inventor exclusive rights to make, use or sell the invention for a fixed period.
keyPoints: Copyright protects original literary, artistic, musical or software works, giving the creator exclusive rights over reproduction and distribution.
A trademark protects distinctive brand names, logos or symbols that identify a company's goods or services.
A patent protects new inventions, giving the inventor exclusive rights to make, use or sell the invention for a fixed period.

text: How can we embed audio in a web page using HTML? Give example.

Example:
<audio src="music.mp3" controls>
Your browser does not support the audio element.
</audio>

Alternatively, <embed> tag can also be used: <embed src="audio.mp3" width="300" height="50">

text: How is CSS beneficial for web development? (any two points)
modelAnswer: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) is beneficial for web development because: (1) Separation of content and presentation — HTML handles structure while CSS handles styling, making code cleaner and easier to maintain. (2) Consistent styling — one CSS file can style multiple web pages, ensuring uniformity across a website. (3) Faster page loading — by reusing styles, less code needs to be loaded. (4) Easier maintenance — changing one CSS file updates the appearance of the entire website.
keyPoints: Separation of content (HTML) and presentation (CSS)
Consistent styling across multiple pages from a single CSS file
Faster page loading due to reusable styles
Easy maintenance: one change in CSS updates the whole site

text: What is CSS and why is it used in web designing?
modelAnswer: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) is a stylesheet language used to describe the visual presentation/appearance of HTML documents. It controls the layout, colors, fonts, spacing, and overall design of web pages. It is used in web designing because: (1) It separates content (HTML) from presentation (CSS), making code cleaner and easier to maintain. (2) One CSS file can style multiple pages, ensuring consistent appearance across a website without repeating styles in each HTML file.
keyPoints: CSS: Cascading Style Sheets — controls visual presentation of web pages

text: What is e-Banking? Mention one difference between e-Banking and e-Shopping.
modelAnswer:
e-Banking (Electronic Banking / Online Banking): The use of the Internet and digital technology to access bank accounts, transfer funds, pay bills, check balance, and perform other banking transactions without physically visiting a bank branch.

e-Banking: Used for financial/banking services such as money transfer, bill payment, and account management.
e-Shopping: Used for buying products and services online through e-commerce portals like Amazon, Flipkart, etc.

text: Write any two differences between the Outline and Border-style properties of CSS.
modelAnswer:
1. Border is part of the box model and occupies space (affects layout). Outline is drawn outside the border and does NOT occupy space, so it does not affect the layout of surrounding elements.
2. Border can be applied to individual sides (border-top, border-right, border-bottom, border-left). Outline is always drawn on all four sides at once — individual sides cannot be set separately.
3. Border can be rounded using border-radius. Outline does not support border-radius.
keyPoints: Border: occupies space, part of box model; Outline: does not occupy space
Border: can be set for individual sides; Outline: applied to all 4 sides at once
Border supports border-radius (rounded); Outline does not
Outline is often used for accessibility/focus indicators without affecting layout

text: Expand the following in the context of Internet Protocols: (a) SMTP (b) POP3. Also write the difference between SMTP and POP3.
modelAnswer:
(a) SMTP: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
(b) POP3: Post Office Protocol (version 3)

Difference:
SMTP is used to SEND emails from a client to the mail server and between servers. POP3 is used to RECEIVE / download emails from the mail server to the client's local device. SMTP pushes mail; POP3 pulls mail.
keyPoints: SMTP: Simple Mail Transfer Protocol
POP3: Post Office Protocol version 3
SMTP: used for sending emails (client→server, server→server)
POP3: used for receiving/downloading emails (server→client)

text: What is e-Governance? Explain any two merits of e-Governance.
modelAnswer:
e-Governance: The use of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) by the government to deliver public services, share information, and communicate with citizens efficiently and transparently.

Merits:
1. 24×7 Availability — Government services are accessible anytime and from anywhere, without needing to visit a government office in person.
2. Cost and time saving — Citizens save time and travel costs; government processes become more efficient and paperless.
3. Transparency — Digital records reduce corruption and increase accountability in government processes.
keyPoints: e-Governance: use of ICT by government to deliver services
Merit 1: 24×7 availability of services online
Merit 2: Cost and time saving for citizens and government
Merit 3: Transparency and reduced corruption

text: Differentiate between a Web Address and an Email Address. Write an example of each. OR Expand the terms SMS and MMS in context of Mobile Technologies. Differentiate between SMS and MMS.
modelAnswer:
Web Address vs Email Address:
A Web Address (URL) is the address of a website/web page on the Internet (e.g., https://www.google.com). An Email Address is the unique address used to send and receive electronic mail (e.g., student@school.edu). Web addresses use http/https; email addresses use the '@' symbol to separate username from domain.

OR

SMS: Short Message Service — text-only messages, up to 160 characters.
MMS: Multimedia Messaging Service — messages with multimedia content (images, audio, video).
Difference: SMS can send only plain text. MMS can send text along with multimedia content like photos, audio clips, and videos. MMS messages are typically larger in size than SMS.
keyPoints: Web Address (URL): address of a website — e.g., https://www.google.com
Email Address: address for emails with '@' — e.g., user@domain.com
SMS: Short Message Service — text only, up to 160 characters
MMS: Multimedia Messaging Service — text + images/audio/video
